instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Get employees earning above average salary
output: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Get the employee with the highest salary
output: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary = (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id), departments(id, dept_name)
Get employees in the Engineering department
output: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE department_id = (SELECT id FROM departments WHERE dept_name = 'Engineering');

instruction:
Schema: orders(id, user_id, total)
Get users who placed orders over 500
output: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT user_id FROM orders WHERE total > 500);

instruction:
Schema: products(id, name, price, category)
Get products more expensive than the average in their category
output: SELECT * FROM products p WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products WHERE category = p.category);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa)
Get students with GPA above the minimum GPA of grade A students
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE gpa > (SELECT MIN(gpa) FROM students WHERE grade = 'A');

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary)
Get employees who earn more than employee id 5
output: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT salary FROM employees WHERE id = 5);

instruction:
Schema: departments(id, dept_name), employees(id, name, department_id, salary)
Get departments that have at least one employee
output: SELECT * FROM departments WHERE id IN (SELECT department_id FROM employees);

instruction:
Schema: departments(id, dept_name), employees(id, name, department_id)
Get departments with no employees
output: SELECT * FROM departments WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT department_id FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL);

instruction:
Schema: users(id, name), orders(id, user_id, total)
Get users who have never ordered
output: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT user_id FROM orders);

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Get each employee with their department average salary
output: SELECT e.name, e.salary, d.avg_sal FROM employees e JOIN (SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) AS avg_sal FROM employees GROUP BY department_id) d ON e.department_id = d.department_id;

instruction:
Schema: products(id, name, price)
Get the second highest priced product
output: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = (SELECT MAX(price) FROM products WHERE price < (SELECT MAX(price) FROM products));

instruction:
Schema: scores(student_id, exam_id, score)
Get students who scored above average on exam 1
output: SELECT * FROM scores WHERE exam_id = 1 AND score > (SELECT AVG(score) FROM scores WHERE exam_id = 1);

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary)
Check if any employee earns more than 100000
output: SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees WHERE salary > 100000);

instruction:
Schema: orders(id, user_id, total, status)
Get users whose all orders are completed
output: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT user_id FROM orders WHERE status != 'completed');

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, department_id, salary)
Get employees earning more than anyone in department 2
output: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > ALL (SELECT salary FROM employees WHERE department_id = 2);

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, department_id, salary)
Get employees earning more than someone in department 2
output: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > ANY (SELECT salary FROM employees WHERE department_id = 2);

instruction:
Schema: customers(id, name), orders(id, customer_id, total)
Get customers with order totals matching the maximum single order
output: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE total = (SELECT MAX(total) FROM orders));

instruction:
Schema: items(id, name, category_id), categories(id, name)
Get items in categories that start with 'E'
output: SELECT * FROM items WHERE category_id IN (SELECT id FROM categories WHERE name LIKE 'E%');

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Get the top earner in each department
output: SELECT * FROM employees e WHERE salary = (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE department_id = e.department_id);

instruction:
Schema: accounts(id, balance, user_id), users(id, name)
Get users with balance above the overall average balance
output: SELECT u.name FROM users u JOIN accounts a ON u.id = a.user_id WHERE a.balance > (SELECT AVG(balance) FROM accounts);

instruction:
Schema: movies(id, title, rating)
Get movies rated higher than the average comedy rating
output: SELECT * FROM movies WHERE rating > (SELECT AVG(rating) FROM movies WHERE genre = 'comedy');

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, department_id)
Get departments with exactly 3 employees
output: SELECT department_id FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING COUNT(*) = 3;

instruction:
Schema: orders(id, user_id, total)
Get the user with the most orders
output: SELECT user_id FROM orders GROUP BY user_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1;

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, class_id), classes(id, name)
Get students in classes that have more than 30 students
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE class_id IN (SELECT class_id FROM students GROUP BY class_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 30);
